newsitem.title: USA: American seeks arbitration with pilots.
newsitem.headline: American seeks arbitration with pilots.

text.p: American Airlines President Don Carty on Tuesday said the company had sent a letter to the pilots' union seeking arbitration to resolve their escalating contract dispute.

"We believe arbitration is the only rational solution to the dilemma," Carty said in a news conference. "If they are confident in their position, they should have absolutely no concern about arbitrating the matter."
The offer appeared to be an olive branch from the airline, which earlier turned down binding arbitration, as did the pilots' union.

The two sides are now in a 30-day "cooling off" period which ends February 15. The pilots, represented by the American Pilot Association, have threatened to strike unless their demands for an 11 percent pay increase and other issues are met.
Carty said the airline, a unit of AMR Corp, did not want a strike, "but we cannot accept APA's demands." The demands would cost American $200 million annually, he said.
"The very fabric of this company is going to be torn apart by a strike," Carty said.
He said the threat of a strike had not yet affected flight bookings, but that it likely would as the deadline neared. He said an earlier strike by flight attendants cost the company $100 million.
